text:
Sebastian Aho's 323rd goal, against the Rangers, made him the Canes' all-time leading goal scorer in the team's own words. It landed in the middle of a season where Carolina looks like the best team in hockey: 19-3-3, 41 points, 8-1-1 in its last 10.

This is not a hot streak dressed up. The Hurricanes get 60% of the expected goals overall (the quality of chances for and against) and 59% at 5v5. They outshoot and out-chance almost everyone. There is some luck in the record, about 4.6 points above what the chances earned, mostly from goaltending, but our simulations still project 121 points and a 90% chance at the division.

The depth is the scary part. Aho's line with Andrei Svechnikov and William Carrier gets 65% of the chances. The kids' line of Logan Stankoven, Jackson Blake and Nikolaj Ehlers has outscored teams 14-1 at 5v5 with 72% of the expected goals. Stankoven has 12 points in his last 10.

There are small worries. Ehlers has been ruled out of recent games with an injury. Jordan Staal's struggles have drawn headlines, and Wednesday's win in Tampa, as North State Journal's Cory Lavalette put it, was one where Bussi stole two points. Taylor Hall was honored for his 1,000th game. What to watch: whether Ehlers returns soon, because that line is the one nobody else has an answer for.
headline: Aho owns the record book, Carolina owns the league
